# GikyMessage

> GikyMessage is a text format for Minecraft messages on Paper, Velocity and other Adventure
> platforms. A plugin compiles each string once and renders it into an Adventure component. This
> file is a complete reference for AI assistants: the syntax, the rules for writing GikyMessage
> strings, and the rules for converting MiniMessage and legacy `&`/`§` strings to GikyMessage.

Applies to GikyMessage 1.0.0-rc.2. Every GikyMessage example in this file was compiled and rendered
with that version. Documentation for people:
https://github.com/groundbreakingmc/GikyMessage/tree/main/wiki

## Rules for the assistant

1. Every message you write must be valid GikyMessage: no MiniMessage tags, `§` codes or JSON may
   remain.
2. Keep the visible text exactly: same words, language, punctuation and spaces. Do not translate or
   rephrase it.
3. Placeholder keys are defined by the plugin and are case-sensitive. Keep them as they are; never
   invent keys. Convert other placeholder syntaxes (`<player>`, `%player%`) to `{player}` and say
   that you did.
4. In a YAML file, change only the message values; keep keys, comments and structure. Wrap every
   message in single quotes and write an apostrophe as `''`. Never use double quotes: YAML rejects
   `\[` inside them.
5. A list (item lore, multi-line messages) stays a list; convert each line on its own.
6. When something has no GikyMessage equivalent (section 7.3), convert the rest and tell the user
   what was dropped or approximated.
7. Prefer the simplest form: `&` codes for colors, `[...]` only where a scope, an action or a
   condition is needed.
8. Check the result against the checklist at the end of this file before answering.

## 1. Codes

| Write | Effect |
|---|---|
| `&0`…`&9`, `&a`…`&f` | Named color (table below). Codes are case-insensitive. |
| `&#RRGGBB`, `#RRGGBB` | Hex color, always six digits. The `&` is optional. |
| `&l` `&o` `&n` `&m` `&k` | Bold, italic, underlined, strikethrough, obfuscated. |
| `&r` | Plain text: no color, decorations or shadow. Inside a segment it also cancels the style inherited from outside; the segment's click and hover stay. |
| `$#RRGGBB`, `$RRGGBB` | Opaque text shadow in that color, always six digits. The `#` is optional. |
| `$#RRGGBB:AA` | Shadow with alpha after a colon: `00` transparent … `ff` opaque. |
| `$#000000:00` | No shadow. |

- A color code does NOT end decorations: in `&6&lSkyCraft &7survival` the word "survival" is gray
  and still bold. End decorations with `&r` or scope them: `[&6&lSkyCraft] &7survival`.
- A color or shadow lasts until the next color or shadow code, `&r`, or the end of the enclosing
  `[...]`. A decoration lasts until `&r` or the end of the enclosing `[...]`.
- `&`, `#` or `$` that does not start a valid code is literal: `Tom & Jerry`, `#1`, `$5`.
- A hex code is exactly six `0-9a-fA-F` digits and has no shorter form: `&#f80` and `$#f80` are
  literal text. The text after a code can start with any character: `&#ff8800Bad` is "Bad" in
  orange and `$#ff5555Bad` is "Bad" with a red shadow. Alpha is read only from a colon and two
  digits right after a shadow.
- `#` or `$` followed by six `0-9a-fA-F` characters is always a code, also in the middle of a
  sentence. To show such text, write `\#123456` or `\$100000`.

| Code | Name | Hex |
|---|---|---|
| `&0` | black | `#000000` |
| `&1` | dark_blue | `#0000aa` |
| `&2` | dark_green | `#00aa00` |
| `&3` | dark_aqua | `#00aaaa` |
| `&4` | dark_red | `#aa0000` |
| `&5` | dark_purple | `#aa00aa` |
| `&6` | gold | `#ffaa00` |
| `&7` | gray | `#aaaaaa` |
| `&8` | dark_gray | `#555555` |
| `&9` | blue | `#5555ff` |
| `&a` | green | `#55ff55` |
| `&b` | aqua | `#55ffff` |
| `&c` | red | `#ff5555` |
| `&d` | light_purple | `#ff55ff` |
| `&e` | yellow | `#ffff55` |
| `&f` | white | `#ffffff` |

The names are the ones `color:` and `style:` accept, in any case. `grey` and `dark_grey` are not
accepted.

## 2. Placeholders

- `{key}` is replaced with the value the plugin supplies for `key`.
- A key the plugin does not supply stays as the literal text `{key}`.
- Values are inserted as plain text and never parsed: the value `&cBob` shows as `&cBob`. Only the
  plugin can supply a formatted value, such as a rank prefix.
- An empty value renders as nothing, but the spaces around it stay. Hide them with a condition:
  `[{clan} ](if:{clan}){player}`.
- `{` without a closing `}` is literal.

## 3. Segments

```text
[text](action:value, action:value)
```

- `text` is full GikyMessage: codes, placeholders, nested segments.
- Codes inside `[...]` end at `]`; the style from before the segment continues after it.
- `[text]` without `(...)` only scopes style: in `&7Hello, [&f{player}]!` the name is white, and
  "Hello, " and "!" are gray.
- A segment inherits the style from outside: in `&c[&lWarning:] restart` the word "Warning:" is red
  and bold, "restart" is red.
- `[` always opens a segment. An unclosed `[` closes at the end of the string and is not shown, so
  `:-[` loses its bracket. A `]` without an open `[` is literal.
- `(` directly after `]` starts an action list: `[see](here)` shows only "see". To show such text,
  escape the brackets: `\[see\](here)`.
- Segments nest. An inner segment's click and hover win for its own text:
  `[&7Click [&ehere](run:/spawn) &7now](show:&7Tip)`.
- A segment's `color:`, or a color in its `style:`, applies to everything inside it and overrides
  colors set inside, nested segments included; `style:reset` overrides every style inside. When the
  text has several colors, use `&` codes instead of `color:`.

### 3.1 Action list syntax

- Actions are separated by `,`. Spaces around names and values are trimmed; only `suggest` keeps
  trailing spaces.
- Action names are lowercase and case-sensitive. Unknown names are ignored.
- Quote a value that contains `,` or `)`, with `"…"` or `'…'`.
- A quote opens a quoted value only as the first character of a value. Anywhere else `'` and `"` are
  ordinary characters, so `show:Don't click` needs no quotes. Inside a quoted value the other kind
  of quote is ordinary too: `show:"&7It's free, try it"`.
- Inside quotes `\"` and `\'` give a quote and `\\` gives `\`. Every other backslash stays, so `\n`,
  `\[` and the other escapes of section 6 work inside quotes as they do without them. A quoted value
  keeps its leading and trailing spaces.
- Repeated actions: `color` and `style` use the first occurrence; other actions use the last one,
  except `if` in a segment with branches (section 4).
- One click per segment. With several click actions the winner is `run`, then `suggest`, `url`,
  `copy`, `page`.
- One content action per segment: `head`, then `sprite`, `lang`.

### 3.2 Actions

| Action | Value | `{key}` in value | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | command, e.g. `/spawn` | yes | Click: the player runs the command. |
| `suggest` | text | yes | Click: puts the text into the chat input. Trailing spaces are kept. |
| `url` | full address with `https://` or `http://` | yes | Click: opens the link. A fixed invalid address is a load error; an invalid address from a placeholder drops the click. |
| `copy` | text | yes | Click: copies the text. |
| `page` | page number, 1 or more | no | Click: turns the book to that page. |
| `show` | GikyMessage text | yes | Hover tooltip. Codes, placeholders, segments and `\n` work inside. |
| `insert` | text | no, `{key}` stays literal | Shift-click: inserts the text into the chat input. |
| `color` | `red`, `c`, `&c`, `#ff5555`, `&#ff5555`, `&x&f&f&5&5&5&5`, or a gradient: two or more of them joined by `-` without spaces, e.g. `#ff5555-#5555ff` or `red-blue` | yes | Color of the whole segment, overriding colors inside it. A gradient colors the characters along its colors and keeps decorations. An invalid value is ignored. |
| `style` | words separated by spaces: `bold` `italic` `underlined` (or `underline`) `strikethrough` `obfuscated` `reset`, color names, `&` codes; e.g. `style:"gold bold"` | yes | Style of the whole segment. `reset` means white with every decoration explicitly off; later words apply on top: `style:"reset gray"`. |
| `phase` | number, a full loop is `1` | no | Shifts the colors of the segment's gradients along the text; `0` and `1` look the same, negative values move the other way. |
| `font` | resource key; the namespace defaults to `minecraft` | no | Font: `font:uniform`. |
| `head` | player name | yes | Replaces the segment with that player's head (Minecraft 1.21.9+). If a name from a placeholder can't belong to a player (spaces, more than 16 characters), the segment's text is shown instead; a fixed invalid name is a load error. |
| `sprite` | key of a texture in the blocks atlas: `block/stone`; a resource pack's `assets/myserver/textures/block/coin.png` is `myserver:block/coin` | no | Replaces the segment with that texture (Minecraft 1.21.9+). Only the blocks atlas is used; item textures are in a separate atlas since Minecraft 1.21.11. |
| `lang` | translation key: `item.minecraft.diamond` | yes | Text in each player's game language. The segment text is the fallback for clients without the key (shown on Minecraft 1.19.4+). The style at the start of the segment text applies to the whole translation; codes later inside it are dropped. An empty key leaves plain text. |
| `if`, `unless` | condition (section 4) | yes | Shows or hides the segment, or picks a branch. |
| `transform` | steps (section 5) | no | Changes the segment's text. |

## 4. Conditions

- `[{clan} ](if:{clan})` — shown while `{clan}` has text.
- `[&7no clan](unless:{clan})` — shown while `{clan}` is empty.
- `[&6VIP ](if:{group}==vip)` and `[&7(away) ](if:{status}!=online)` — compare two values, or a
  value with fixed text.
- `[&aonline|&7offline](if:{status}==online)` — branches: the first is shown when the condition
  holds, the second otherwise.
- `[&4Owner|&cAdmin|&9Moderator|&7Player](if:{group}==owner, if:{group}==admin, if:{group}==mod)` —
  the n-th condition decides the n-th branch; the last branch is the fallback.
- `[&6VIP ](if:{group}==vip || {group}==mvp)` — `||` means or.
- `[&a\[Claim\]](if:{level}>=10 && {claimed}!=yes, run:/reward claim)` — `&&` means and.
- `&7Ping: [&a{ping}|&e{ping}|&c{ping}](if:{ping}<100, if:{ping}<250)` — `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`
  compare numbers.
- `[&6VIP ](if:{vip}, unless:{vanished})` — `if` and `unless` together: both must hold.

Rules:
- Empty means empty text or only spaces. Numbers, `0` included, count as text. An unknown key
  renders as `{key}` and counts as text.
- `==` and `!=` compare the plain text of both sides, colors ignored; spaces around the sides are
  trimmed; case matters. When both sides are numbers they compare by value: `10.0==10` holds.
- A number is an optional `+` or `-`, digits, and optionally `.` and more digits. `<`, `>`, `<=`,
  `>=` hold only when both sides are numbers; empty values, `1,000`, `1.2K` and `1e3` are not
  numbers.
- `&&` binds tighter than `||`: `{a} || {b} && {c}` means a, or both b and c. There are no
  parentheses; nest segments for more complex logic.
- `unless` negates the whole condition: `unless:{a} || {b}` shows the segment while neither holds.
- Operators are read from the message only; `&&`, `||` or `==` inside a placeholder's value are
  plain text.
- `=` alone is not an operator: `if:{group}=vip` compares nothing and always holds. Write `==`.
- Without branches, a segment uses only its last `if` and its last `unless`.
- `|` splits branches only in a segment that has a condition; write `\|` for a literal `|` there.
  Elsewhere `|` is literal.
- The segment's other actions apply to whichever branch is shown.
- A condition without placeholders is decided when the message is loaded.
- Keep the spaces that belong to an optional part inside its brackets.

## 5. Transforms

`transform:compact`; several steps are separated by spaces: `transform:"smallcaps max:10"`.

| Step | Effect |
|---|---|
| `compact` | Every standalone number of 1000 or more is shortened with `K`, `M`, `B`, `T`, one decimal, rounded half up: `1234567` → `1.2M`, `1000` → `1K`, `999999` → `1M`. Digits glued to letters (`Steve1234`) are untouched. |
| `upper`, `lower` | Upper or lower case. |
| `smallcaps` | Latin `a`–`z` become small capitals: `Steve` → `ꜱᴛᴇᴠᴇ`. `x` and non-Latin letters stay as they are. |
| `max:N` | Keeps at most N characters of the whole segment, without an ellipsis. |

Steps run from left to right, `max` always last. Transforms run before gradients and `lang`.
Unknown steps are ignored.

## 6. Escapes

- `\[` `\]` → `[` `]`
- `\{` `\}` → `{` `}`
- `\\` → `\`
- `\n` → line break
- `\|` → `|`, needed only inside a segment with a condition
- `\&` `\#` `\$` → `&` `#` `$`, needed where the sign would start a code: `R\&D`, `\#123456`,
  `\$100000`
- Any other backslash stays as written: `a\qb` shows `a\qb`.
- `<` and `>` are plain text.

## 7. Converting from MiniMessage

### 7.1 Procedure

The MiniMessage format itself: https://docs.papermc.io/adventure/minimessage/format/

1. Read the MiniMessage string as nested tags. Unclosed tags end at the end of the string; `<reset>`
   closes every open tag.
2. Escape the literal text for GikyMessage: `[` `]` `{` `}` `\` become `\[` `\]` `\{` `\}` `\\`; an
   `&` directly followed by a letter, a digit or `#` becomes `\&`; a `#` or `$` directly followed by
   six `0-9a-fA-F` characters becomes `\#` or `\$`; MiniMessage's `\<` becomes `<`.
3. Tags that are not standard MiniMessage tags are the plugin's placeholders: `<player>` →
   `{player}`.
4. Colors and decorations become `&` codes where the tag opens. A closing tag becomes the end of a
   `[...]` scope: `<red>Error</red> details` → `[&cError] details`. The scope can be left out where
   the following text sets its own color anyway and no decoration was active.
5. Click, hover, insert, font, gradient, rainbow, lang, head and sprite tags become actions of a
   segment around the text they wrap. Tags that wrap the same text become one segment with several
   actions. Ranges that overlap without nesting are split into several segments.
6. Convert hover text recursively into a `show:` value. Quote it when it contains `,` or `)` or
   starts with a quote (section 3.1); inside the quotes write a quote of the same kind as `\"` or
   `\'`.
7. Write each result in YAML single quotes.

### 7.2 Tag map

| MiniMessage | GikyMessage |
|---|---|
| `<black>` … `<white>`, `<color:red>`, `<colour:red>`, `<c:red>` | `&0` … `&f` by the name table; `<grey>` is `&7`, `<dark_grey>` is `&8` |
| `<#ff8800>`, `<color:#ff8800>` | `&#ff8800` |
| `</red>`, `</color>`, `</#ff8800>`, `</bold>` and other closing tags | end of a `[...]` scope |
| `<bold>`, `<b>` | `&l` |
| `<italic>`, `<i>`, `<em>` | `&o` |
| `<underlined>`, `<u>` | `&n` |
| `<strikethrough>`, `<st>` | `&m` |
| `<obfuscated>`, `<obf>` | `&k` |
| `<!bold>`, `<bold:false>`, the same for other decorations | No code. Restructure so the decoration is never on for that text: end it with `]` or with `&r` plus the color again. For item names and lore see section 9. |
| `<reset>` | `&r`; also end any segment that is open at that point |
| `<shadow:black>`, `<shadow:#000000>` | `$#000000:40` (MiniMessage's default alpha 0.25 = `40`) |
| `<shadow:#ff0000:0.5>` | `$#ff0000:80` (alpha × 255 as two hex digits: 0.25 → `40`, 0.5 → `80`, 1 → `ff`) |
| `<shadow:#ff000080>` | `$#ff0000:80` |
| `<!shadow>` | `$#000000:00` |
| `<click:run_command:/spawn>` | `run:/spawn` |
| `<click:suggest_command:'/msg Steve '>` | `suggest:/msg Steve ` |
| `<click:open_url:'https://example.com'>` | `url:https://example.com` |
| `<click:copy_to_clipboard:play.example.com>` | `copy:play.example.com` |
| `<click:change_page:2>` | `page:2` |
| `<hover:show_text:'…'>` | `show:…` |
| `<insert:text>` | `insert:text` |
| `<font:uniform>`, `<font:minecraft:uniform>` | `font:uniform` |
| `<newline>`, `<br>` | `\n` |
| `<gradient:#5e4fa2:#f79459>` | `color:#5e4fa2-#f79459` |
| `<gradient:red:blue>` | `color:red-blue`, names by the name table |
| `<gradient:red>` with one color | `&c` |
| `<gradient:…:0.5>`, `<rainbow:2>` with a phase | Drop the phase: the scales differ. For animation frames use `phase:` values from 0 to just below 1. |
| `<rainbow>` | `color:#ff0000-#ffff00-#00ff00-#00ffff-#0000ff-#ff00ff` (approximation) |
| `<rainbow:!>` | the same stops in reverse order |
| `<transition:…:phase>` | one fixed color `&#RRGGBB`: the color at that phase |
| `<pride>`, `<pride:flag>` | `color:` with the flag's colors joined by `-` (approximation) |
| `<lang:key>`, `<tr:key>`, `<translate:key>` | `[](lang:key)` |
| `<lang_or:key:Fallback>` | `[Fallback](lang:key)` |
| `<head:Steve>` | `[](head:Steve)`; with a placeholder `[{player}](head:{player})` |
| `<sprite:block/stone>`, `<sprite:blocks:block/stone>` | `[](sprite:block/stone)` |
| `<player>` and other plugin tags | `{player}` |
| `\<` | `<` |

### 7.3 No equivalent

Drop these and tell the user: `<hover:show_item:…>`, `<hover:show_entity:…>`, `<key:…>` keybinds,
`<selector:…>`, `<score:…>`, `<nbt:…>`/`<data:…>`, translation arguments (`<lang:key:arg…>` keeps
only the key), `<click:show_dialog:…>` and `<click:custom:…>`, `<head:…>` with a UUID, a texture or
an `outer_layer` argument, `<sprite:…>` from an atlas other than blocks (such as `items`), and
custom plugin tags that are more than plain placeholders. A plugin can often supply such content as
a placeholder value instead.

### 7.4 Examples

| MiniMessage | GikyMessage |
|---|---|
| `<gray>Hello, <white><player></white>!` | `&7Hello, [&f{player}]!` |
| `<red><bold>Warning:</bold> the server restarts in <time>` | `&c[&lWarning:] the server restarts in {time}` |
| `<red><bold>Alert<reset>: restart in <time>` | `&c&lAlert&r: restart in {time}` |
| `<b>Bold</b> normal <i>italic</i>` | `[&lBold] normal [&oitalic]` |
| `<gray>[<gold>VIP</gold>] <white><player>` | `&7\[&6VIP&7\] &f{player}` |
| `<gradient:#55ffff:#5555ff><bold>SkyCraft</bold></gradient> <gray>» <white>Welcome!` | `[&lSkyCraft](color:#55ffff-#5555ff) &7» &fWelcome!` |
| `<click:run_command:/spawn><hover:show_text:'<green>Click to teleport'><gold>[Spawn]</gold></hover></click>` | `[&6\[Spawn\]](run:/spawn, show:&aClick to teleport)` |
| `<gray>Join our <click:open_url:'https://discord.gg/example'><blue><u>Discord</u></blue></click>!` | `&7Join our [&9&nDiscord](url:https://discord.gg/example)!` |
| `<hover:show_text:'<gold><player><newline><gray>Rank: <rank>'><player></hover>` | `[{player}](show:&6{player}\n&7Rank: {rank})` |
| `<hover:show_text:'<gray>Rules: be nice, no spam<newline>No cheats'><yellow>[?]</yellow></hover>` | `[&e\[?\]](show:"&7Rules: be nice, no spam\nNo cheats")` |
| `<red>Line one<newline><gray>Line two` | `&cLine one\n&7Line two` |
| `<shadow:black>Shadowed</shadow> text` | `[$#000000:40Shadowed] text` |
| `<gray>You found <lang_or:item.minecraft.diamond:Diamond>!` | `&7You found [Diamond](lang:item.minecraft.diamond)!` |
| `<rainbow>Rainbow text</rainbow>` | `[Rainbow text](color:#ff0000-#ffff00-#00ff00-#00ffff-#0000ff-#ff00ff)` |
| `<gray>R&D team` | `&7R\&D team` |

A YAML file before and after:

```yaml
join: "<gray>[<green>+</green>] <white><player> joined"
```

```yaml
join: '&7\[&a+&7\] &f{player} joined'
```

## 8. Converting from legacy `&` and `§` codes

1. `§` becomes `&`.
2. Hex colors in other notations become `&#RRGGBB`: `&x&f&f&8&8&0&0` (or with `§`), `<#ff8800>`,
   `{#ff8800}`. `&#ff8800` and `#ff8800` stay.
3. In legacy text a color code switches decorations off; in GikyMessage it does not. Where a color
   code follows an active `&l` `&o` `&n` `&m` or `&k`, put `&r` right before it. A decoration placed
   directly before a color code had no effect in legacy text; drop it.
4. Escape literal `[` `]` `{` `}` `\`, and a `#` or `$` followed by six `0-9a-fA-F` characters that
   is meant as text, such as the price `$100000` (section 6).
5. Placeholders in other syntaxes become the keys the plugin supplies: `%player%` → `{player}`.

| Legacy | GikyMessage |
|---|---|
| `&6&lSkyCraft &7» &fWelcome, %player%!` | `&6&lSkyCraft &r&7» &fWelcome, {player}!` |
| `§cError: §7unknown command` | `&cError: &7unknown command` |
| `&x&f&f&8&8&0&0Orange` | `&#ff8800Orange` |
| `&8[&6VIP&8] &f%player%` | `&8\[&6VIP&8\] &f{player}` |
| `&l&6Title` | `&6Title` |

## 9. Item names and lore

Minecraft shows item names and lore in italic unless italic is explicitly switched off, and
GikyMessage has no code that switches it off; `&r` does not. Prefer to let the plugin remove the
default italic in code with `decorationIfAbsent(TextDecoration.ITALIC, TextDecoration.State.FALSE)`.
If it must happen in the text, give every run of one color its own segment whose `style:` is `reset`
plus that color, because `style:reset` turns all decorations off but also overrides colors inside
the segment:

```text
[Deals ](style:"reset gray")[+5](style:"reset red")[ damage](style:"reset gray")
```

## 10. Writing new messages

```text
&8\[&6Shop&8\] &7You bought &f{amount}x {item} &7for &6{price} coins&7.
[&a&l\[ACCEPT\]](run:/tpaccept, show:&aAccept the request) [&c&l\[DENY\]](run:/tpdeny, show:&cDeny the request)
&7Join our [&9&nDiscord](url:https://discord.gg/example, show:&7Open the invite)&7!
[&e{player}](suggest:/msg {player} , show:&7Send a private message)
[&7\[{clan}\] ](if:{clan})&f{player}&7: {message}
&f{friend} [&aonline|&7offline](if:{status}==online)
&7Balance: &e[{balance}](transform:compact) &7coins
[&lSkyCraft](color:#55ffff-#5555ff)
&6&lSkyCraft&r\n&7Welcome back, &f{player}&7!
&7You found a [&bDiamond](lang:item.minecraft.diamond)&7!
[{player}](head:{player}) &f{player} &7joined the game
```

- Use only the placeholders the plugin documents.
- Tell the player what a click does, in a short tooltip.
- Never expect a placeholder value to carry formatting.

## 11. Plugin code

| MiniMessage API | GikyMessage API |
|---|---|
| `MiniMessage.miniMessage().deserialize(s)` on every send | `Text<Void> text = Text.of(s);` once, then `text.render()` on every send |
| `Placeholder.unparsed("player", name)` | a handler that calls `value.text(name)` |
| `Placeholder.component("item", component)` | `value.component(component)` |
| `Placeholder.parsed("prefix", miniMessageString)` | `value.component(miniMessageString, MINI)` with a constant `MINI = MiniMessage.miniMessage()::deserialize` |
| `Formatter.number("amount", n)` | `value.number(n)` for whole numbers; format other numbers yourself and use `value.text(...)` |
| custom `TagResolver` tags | placeholders and segments |

```java
// Once, when the messages are loaded:
Text<Player> join = Text.of(config.getString("join"), key -> switch (key) {
    case "player" -> (player, value) -> value.text(player.getName());
    case "balance" -> (player, value) -> value.number(economy.balance(player));
    default -> null; // keys the plugin doesn't supply stay as {key}
});

// Every time the message is sent:
player.sendMessage(join.render(player));
```

A compiled `Text` can be kept and shared between threads. `Text.of` throws `TextFormatException` for
a message that can't work, such as `url:` with a fixed invalid address.

## 12. Version requirements

| Feature | Adventure on the server | Minecraft on the player's side |
|---|---|---|
| `lang:` | 4.13+ | 1.19.4+ to show the fallback text |
| `$#` shadows | 4.18+ | 1.21.4+ |
| `head:`, `sprite:` | 4.25+ | 1.21.9+ |

On an older Adventure, a message that uses these features fails to load with a
`TextFormatException`.

## Checklist

- No MiniMessage tags or `§` codes are left.
- Literal `[` `]` `{` `}` `\` in visible text are escaped; an `&` before a letter, digit or `#`, and
  a `#` or `$` before six hex characters, are written `\&`, `\#`, `\$` when they are meant as text.
- Every segment is closed with `]`, and every `(` after `]` has its `)`.
- Values with `,` or `)` are quoted, and a quote inside them is written `\"` or `\'`.
- A segment has at most one click action.
- Gradients have at least two colors joined by `-`, with no spaces around it.
- `color:` and `style:` use `gray` and `dark_gray`, never `grey`.
- Hex colors and shadows have exactly six digits, and a shadow's alpha follows a colon:
  `$#000000:80`.
- Decorations end where the source ended them: `]` or `&r`.
- Optional parts keep their spaces inside their brackets.
- Placeholder keys match the plugin's keys exactly.
- YAML values are in single quotes, with `''` for an apostrophe.
- Everything dropped or approximated is reported to the user.
